questions.q: Why is the CI/CD pipeline itself considered a security target, not just a tool?
options: Because pipelines are never connected to production systems
Because a compromised pipeline has standing access to deploy, pull secrets, and push images — everything a legitimate deploy can do
Because pipelines cannot run any of Chapter 4's scans
Because only application code can ever be compromised
questions.explain: A pipeline with deploy access, secrets access, and image-push access is a high-value target — compromising it can do everything a legitimate deployment could do, often without the scans or reviews a normal change would go through.

questions.q: What does a required reviewer protection rule on a GitHub Actions environment do?
options: Automatically scans the deployed container image
Pauses a deploy job targeting that environment until a named person or team approves it
Deletes the environment if a deploy fails
Encrypts all secrets used by the pipeline
questions.explain: Required reviewers add a human checkpoint: a deploy job waits for an approval from a named reviewer before it's allowed to proceed against that environment.

questions.q: What does "Start all waiting jobs" represent in GitHub Actions deployment protection rules?
options: A silent, unlogged way to skip all security controls
A visible, logged action that bypasses a waiting protection rule, used deliberately (e.g., for an urgent hotfix)
The default behavior for every deployment, with no approval ever required
A command that deletes all pending deployments
questions.explain: Bypassing a deployment protection rule is supported, but it's an explicit, visible, logged action rather than a quiet workaround — preserving an audit trail of who overrode the gate.

questions.q: Why does pinning a third-party GitHub Action to a commit SHA matter, rather than referencing a mutable tag?
options: SHA pinning makes workflows run faster
A mutable tag can be repointed to different code later, so pinning to a SHA prevents a compromised or changed action from silently altering pipeline behavior
GitHub Actions only supports SHA references, never tags
SHA pinning is required for required reviewers to function
questions.explain: A tag can be moved to point at different code at any time, but a commit SHA is immutable — pinning to it ensures the action's behavior can't change underneath the pipeline without an explicit update.

questions.q: Which earlier chapters' principles does this lesson say should apply directly to the pipeline's own configuration?
options: Chapter 2's least-privilege identity and Chapter 3's secrets management
Chapter 1's shift-left mindset only, with no connection to identity or secrets
None — pipeline security is treated as fully separate from earlier chapters
Only Chapter 4's scanning, with no identity or secrets considerations
questions.explain: Securing the pipeline means applying least-privilege workload identity (Chapter 2) and pulling secrets at runtime from a vault rather than storing them statically (Chapter 3), directly to the pipeline's own configuration.
